cases.title: A saved order appears in the list
cases.given: The app is running with an empty database and the page is opened at 127.0.0.1 with no login
cases.when: The user fills in name "Ana Silva", phone "+351 912 345 678", cake "Chocolate, 2 kg, Happy Birthday Ana", a pickup date tomorrow and time 10:30, and clicks Save
then: The page opened without any login or password prompt
Within 3 seconds the list shows one order with exactly those values
The database holds exactly one order

cases.title: The list sorts upcoming orders first and past orders below
cases.given: Saved orders with pickup dates next Saturday, next Friday, and last Monday (none picked up)
then: The upcoming section lists Friday then Saturday
The last Monday order is in the bottom section

cases.title: Picked up greys an order out and moves it down
cases.when: The user clicks "Picked up" on the first one and reloads the page
then: That order is greyed out in the bottom section
The other order is still at the top
The database marks only the first order as picked up

cases.title: Editing the pickup date updates and re-sorts the order
cases.given: Upcoming orders for Saturday ("Ana") and Sunday ("Bruno")
cases.when: The user clicks "Edit" on Ana's order, changes the date to the Monday after, and saves
then: The list shows Ana's order with the new date below Bruno's
The database holds the new date and still exactly two orders

cases.title: Delete asks first; Cancel keeps, confirm removes
cases.when: The user clicks "Delete" and chooses Cancel, then clicks "Delete" again and confirms
then: An "Are you sure?" confirmation appears each time
After Cancel the order is unchanged in the list and the database
After confirming the order is gone from the list and the database

cases.title: An empty required field saves nothing and keeps the typed text
cases.given: The form with phone, cake and pickup date filled in and the name left empty (repeated for each of the four required fields)
then: Nothing is saved
The empty field is highlighted
The other fields still hold what was typed

cases.title: A pickup date in the past is rejected
cases.given: A fully filled form with a pickup date of yesterday
then: A message says the pickup date is in the past
The database still holds no order

cases.title: A phone number with letters is rejected
cases.given: A fully filled form with phone "91234abc"
then: A message says the phone may contain only digits, spaces and +
Nothing is saved
The same form with phone "+351 912 345 678" is accepted

cases.title: Clicking Save twice saves one order
then: The list shows exactly one order
The database holds exactly one order

cases.title: An unwritable database shows an error and keeps the form
cases.given: The app running with one saved order and the database made unwritable
cases.when: The user saves a valid new order
then: The page shows a clear error
The form still holds the typed values
The database still holds only the first order

cases.title: Orders survive a restart
cases.given: Three saved orders, one of them marked picked up
cases.when: The app process is stopped and started again
then: The list shows the same three orders with the same values and picked-up status

cases.title: Another device cannot open the app
cases.when: A request is made to the laptop's network address (not 127.0.0.1) on the app's port
then: The connection is refused
The server code opens no outbound network connection

cases.title: Today's orders count as upcoming and timed orders sort first
cases.given: Orders for today 15:00, today with no time, today 09:00, and yesterday (not picked up)
cases.when: The page is opened, and a new order for today is saved
then: The upcoming section lists today 09:00, today 15:00, then today with no time
Yesterday's order is in the bottom section
The new order for today is accepted

cases.title: One real day of orders matches the paper notes
cases.given: The app installed on the shop laptop
cases.when: The owner and employee enter one real day of orders while also writing them on paper
then: At the end of the day every paper order is in the list exactly once, with the same details

cases.title: The README explains starting the app and backing up
cases.when: The owner follows it on the shop laptop
then: The app starts and opens in the browser
The owner can copy the database file to a backup location
